type: observable discriminability to identity-indexed omission reconstruction
commonStructure: Both sensor registration and fault-tolerant reconstruction require an injective-enough signature from expected slots to observed records. A count deficit fixes an omission budget; a predictive feature bridge can locate omissions only when competing monotone paths have separated costs.
conditionsForTransfer: Command observables predict image observables across an untouched time block.
A local feature window is distinctive enough that removing one record changes the unique minimum-cost path near the true slot.
Two numerical implementations select stable positions under fixed tolerances.
Synthetic faults reproduce the kinds of deletion, duplication, and drift expected in natural acquisition.
breakConditions: Repeated raster motion and nearly stationary melt-pool appearance make many slots exchangeable.
An 8 by 8 grayscale reduction removes local texture or tail information needed to distinguish adjacent frames.
Count equality hides offsetting deletion and duplication, so the development ordinal pairing is not authenticated.
A model can correlate power with intensity while still failing event identity.
minimumValidation: Recover known singleton deletions first. Missing 127 of 128 singleton cases already makes the aggregate 95 percent gate impossible even if all 1,104 remaining injected deletions were recovered.

evidence.preregisteredPython: 105 of 1,232 deletion identities recovered within one slot; 91.48 percent false-discovery rate.
evidence.independentJavaScript: 1 of 128 singleton deletions recovered; the impossible best-case aggregate recall is 89.69 percent.
evidence.implementationStability: The two implementations call the same singleton slot in 9 of 128 trials; median absolute call difference is 103.5 slots.
evidence.postGateNonlinearDiagnostic: Extra Trees improves singleton recovery to 11 of 128 and dispersed recovery to 45 of 736, still far below the gate and not preregistered.

transferableMethod: Use a fail-fast discriminability screen before natural alignment: quantify cross-block prediction, injected singleton recovery, path-cost margins, and implementation stability. Escalate to natural candidate positions only after all four pass.
validationStatus: The shared identifiability condition is confirmed by a negative result. Transfer of the current 8 by 8 command-image bridge is rejected; no natural slot is adjudicated.
